The paper reports neither number in its text or tables. They only appear as plotted curves in Figure 11 on page 10, so these are my estimates from reading the plot:

- **Contriever recall with 50 documents: about 88–89%.** It's the top dashed orange line, which rises from about 68% at 5 documents and levels off just under 90 (p. 10, Fig. 11).
- **GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) accuracy with 50 documents: about 59–60%.** Its line overlaps longchat-13b-16k's, so this reading is less certain than the recall figure (p. 10, Fig. 11).

What the text does say:
- **Setup:** Contriever, fine-tuned on MS-MARCO, retrieves the top k Wikipedia documents for NaturalQuestions-Open questions. The paper measures retriever recall and reader accuracy, meaning whether any annotated answer appears in the model's output, as k grows (p. 9).
- **Main finding:** reader performance levels off long before retriever recall does. Going from 20 to 50 retrieved documents improves accuracy only about 1.5% for GPT-3.5-Turbo and about 1% for Claude-1.3 (p. 10; also stated on p. 2).

The appendix tables only cover the multi-document QA task, so I couldn't find an exact figure for either value anywhere in the paper.
